title: What's the biggest mistake you made when you first started trading? Let's learn from each other.
author: ExternalMarsupial835
selftext:
Every trader has a story. Maybe it was overtrading, ignoring risk management, chasing FOMO, or letting emotions take control.

What's the one trading mistake that taught you the biggest lesson?

https://app.falkan.in/login

I'm part of the team building FALKAN, a free paper-trading platform currently in beta. We believe learning from mistakes is an important part of becoming a more disciplined trader, and we're interested in hearing real experiences from the trading community.

Let's share lessons, discuss strategies, and help new traders avoid common pitfalls.

Your turn: What was your biggest trading mistake, and what did it teach you?

Disclosure: I'm building FALKAN. We're currently testing the platform and learning from user feedback.

comments.author: dexoyo
comments.body: Biggest mistake > Paper Trading != Real Trading

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: trusting a backtest that filled every order at the bar close. live, the fills came in a tick or two worse almost every time, and the whole edge turned out to be roughly that gap. now nothing goes live until it has run on paper against real quotes for a few weeks.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Mine was sizing up after a hot streak and giving it all back in two days. Paper trading never hurt me because there's no fear in it, real fills and real drawdowns are a different animal entirely.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Trusting a backtest or a short winning streak before counting the trades and costs behind it. Many people tune a strategy until it looks great on past data, then lose money when it meets live fills and a different market. What helps is writing the rules down first, keeping a final period untouched, and trading tiny size for a while. Timing is another trap around earnings and macro releases, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for those) is one source for avoiding it.
